lesson_title: Two Witnesses, One Truth: Reconciling Control Accounts
hook_text: Two records. Two different answers. Neither one is right.
clip_script: Month end. Thabo asks his books one question, two ways. The control account answers: customers owe you R7 440. The pages, added up: R7 130. Three hundred and ten rand apart — somebody is wrong. Here's the twist: it's BOTH of them. Do not pick a favourite witness. Each record travelled its own road, and either road can carry a pothole. Four errors later — a short-added column, a goodbye that never reached the totals, an invoice that never reached a page, two digits that danced — both records, each patched on its own road, say the same thing: R7 500. A number neither of them started with. That's a reconciliation: nobody surrenders; the truth appears where the corrected stories meet.
visual_style: Split screen: two ledger 'witnesses' facing each other across a table, each with a glowing balance; potholes lighting up along two roads beneath them; the balances ticking toward each other until they lock at R7 500.
mood: Detective-case tension resolving into a satisfying click.
pacing: Slow reveal of the difference, quickening through the four findings, landing hard on the meeting point.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and close the case yourself — every rand explained.
